rows.basis: Revenue of the Colocation segment (formerly HPC hosting), all from CoreWeave: 65,424,000 / 319,019,000 total revenue. Digital asset self-mining (229.2M) and hosted mining (24.4M, miner hosting) are excluded. The GPUs are the tenant's.

Revenue of the Colocation segment, 24,378,000 / 510,672,000 total revenue. The same figure appears as 'HPC hosting revenue' (the line's earlier name) and matches the MD&A's stated $24.4M; it is counted once. Mining and miner-hosting revenue are excluded.

Consolidated capex was 729.0M in FY2025 and is not split by segment. The company describes its build-out as converting data centers to HPC hosting for CoreWeave, largely funded by CoreWeave; no AI amount is stated. Construction in progress grew from 112.0M to 911.1M, but that category is not HPC-specific.

Q3 2024 release: up to $1.5M per HPC MW, about $750M, of data-center build-out costs funded by CoreWeave and credited against hosting payments. This supersedes the earlier $575M and covers the whole program, not one fiscal year. It excludes the $104M the company funds for the 70 MW expansion. The $1.14B contractual commitment at 31 Dec 2024 is 'primarily' HPC, so it is a total and is not used.

Q4 2025 release: Core Scientific funds $104M ($1.5M per MW) of powered core and shell for the additional 70 MW CoreWeave expansion, with no capex credit. Only the company-funded part is stated; CoreWeave-funded build costs are not included.

The 2026 releases restate the same $104M company-funded powered core and shell for the 70 MW expansion. This is likely the same spend as the FY2026 row, carried forward, and should not be added to it.
